obtained.how: institutional repository copy: the published article as reprinted (journal layout, pp. 1–10) in M. Greszkiewicz's doctoral dissertation, posted openly by the University of Gdańsk's Institute of Oceanography; only the article's pages (dissertation PDF pp. 46–55) were indexed. The whole dissertation is kept as Greszkiewicz_2021_dissertation.pdf

claims.location: p. 1 (dissertation PDF p. 46), Abstract; p. 3 (PDF p. 48), Table 1; p. 4 (PDF p. 49)
claims.quote: highest rate observed at 22 °C (0.83 mm⋅d−1), a lower rate at 15 °C (0.48
claims.conditions: hatchery eggs reared in recirculating systems (3 tanks per temperature, 10 ± 0.6, 15 ± 0.4, 22 ± 0.5 °C; 15 and 22 °C reached within 24–48 h of hatching), fed dry fodder ad libitum every 1.5 h in the light after yolk-sac absorption; O₂ 7.8 mg/L; slopes of SL at age over days 0–28 from hatching (yolk-sac days included), SL corrected +0.7 mm for shrinkage; 9–27 mm SL; n = 720
claims.note: individual larvae grew up to 1.28 mm/d; growth rose 0.05 mm/d per °C; at 22 °C growth accelerated with age while at 10 and 15 °C it did not (p. 4)

claims.paper: §5.8 (lesson 'An adult set cannot grow a larva')
claims.claim: measured larval growth 0.25–1.21 mm/day from 10 to 24 °C (Górny 1992; Fey & Greszkiewicz 2021)
claims.conditions: as above; Fey & Greszkiewicz supply the 0.25 mm/d at 10 °C (the low end); 1.21 at 24 °C is Górny's
claims.note: mean slope 0.2486 ≈ 0.25 mm/d SL; dry feed, not live zooplankton, so the model's full-ration-of-zooplankton comparison mixes diets

claims.claim: pike larvae fed to excess grow 0.25 (10 °C) … 0.5–0.65 (15) … 0.7–1.0 (21) … mm/d (Górny 1992, Fey & Greszkiewicz 2021)
claims.quote: feeding was conducted ad libitum every 1.5 h during periods with light
claims.note: Fey & Greszkiewicz's points: 0.25 at 10 °C, 0.48 at 15 °C, 0.83 at 22 °C. The 15 °C mean lies just below the comment's 0.5–0.65 band, and the 22 °C value sits in its '21' band; neither changes the comment's point

notes: The same dissertation reprints Greszkiewicz & Fey 2020 (Hydrobiologia 847: 3139–3152), on temperature and cannibalism in larval pike, at its PDF pp. 57 ff. Otolith growth also scaled with somatic growth (sagittae 5.5, 10.9, 20.6 µm/d at 10, 15, 22 °C).
